persistence_invariants.brief: A composite unique constraint on (sku, location) guarantees each SKU at each location is uniquely addressable; a colliding write is rejected at the DB level, never stored as a duplicate (R3).
A CHECK constraint enforces quantity >= 0 so a stored stock level can never go negative; overcommit is rejected at write time before it can persist (R2).
sku, location, quantity, and inventory_code are NOT NULL so every filed stock record durably captures the full set the AC requires.
Each record carries a NOT NULL, immutable created/adjusted timestamp and actor, preserving an unmodifiable audit of who made each inventory adjustment and when (R1).
The Alembic migration that creates the schema is additive and reversible, and existing inventory records created before it survive with no loss across every migration (R1).

nfrs.brief: Existing stock data survives every schema migration with no loss; additive migrations preserve prior inventory records, and each adjustment keeps an unmodifiable timestamp + actor. Defended by a real-branch migration/reversibility integration test (PI4, PI5).

Stock levels never go below zero and never overcommit beyond available quantity; an overcommitting pick is rejected at write time. Owned by the stock service (transactional boundary) and enforced physically by the quantity CHECK constraint (PI2).

Every SKU at every location is uniquely addressable by (sku, location); a collision is resolved at write time, never stored as two duplicates nor surfaced as an error page. Enforced by the composite unique constraint (PI1) and a friendly service-layer conflict response.

Acceptance tests run against the paired Lakebase branch (databricks_postgres via DATABASE_URL), never a mock/in-memory substitute; CI refuses to merge a PR whose integration tests do not run against a real branch. This is the test-strategy contract for AC1.

The UI is a React + TypeScript SPA under client/ that loads once and navigates client-side with no full-page reloads; stock adjustments update the affected row in place (optimistic, reconciled against the server). The backend boundary returns JSON only (renders_via: react), and the client ships its own component tests.
Validation messages are clear and specific, naming the offending field rather than a generic 'bad request'. Owned at the API boundary (cross-cutting validation), never the domain. (PO preference.)
A stock-level row missing optional detail (par level, batch, serial) still renders cleanly, defaulting to an explicit 'not tracked' rather than a null crash or blank region. (PO preference.)
